source.version: IJCAI-25 proceedings paper, Special Track on Human-Centred AI, printed pages 10280-10288 (PDF pp. 1-9). The document bears the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-25) proceedings header; no separate revision date is given.
source.title_on_document: Creative Momentum Transfer: How Timing and Labeling of AI Suggestions Shape Iterative Human Ideation

supplement.holds: No supplementary material or appendix is identified in the complete PDF. The main text contains the reported tests and Table 1 contains standard errors for moderator slopes; no external source of missing treatment-effect precision is named.

paper_design_summary: Adults were randomized to a control receiving no external suggestions or to GPT-4 suggestions introduced early or late and explicitly AI-labeled or unlabeled during two rounds of proposing solutions to urban plastic pollution on a web platform. Experts rated creativity and its components, and embedding comparisons measured each participant's alignment with the AI suggestions. The paper also describes a preparatory stimulus pilot and qualitative interviews with a subset of the main experimental sample.

studies.label: Main five-condition, two-round plastic-pollution ideation experiment

assignment.what_was_assigned: People were assigned to Control, Early-AI Labeled, Early-AI Unlabeled, Late-AI Labeled, or Late-AI Unlabeled. The timing and labeling manipulation is between participants; the same participants completed both rounds. Allocation method and concealment are not described. The online_rct label follows the stated web-platform administration, although recruitment channel and physical setting are not specified.
assignment.quote: These participants were randomly assigned to five conditions:

arms.name: Control
arms.description: No external suggestions in either round (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4).

arms.name: Early-AI Labeled
arms.description: GPT-4 suggestions introduced in Round 1 under AI-generated ideas, with explicit visual labeling. No new external inputs in Round 2; continued visibility of earlier suggestions is not stated (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4).

arms.name: Early-AI Unlabeled
arms.description: The same GPT-4 suggestions introduced in Round 1 under Ideas from others, without explicit AI attribution. No new external inputs in Round 2; continued visibility of earlier suggestions is not stated (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4).

arms.name: Late-AI Labeled
arms.description: No suggestions in Round 1; the same GPT-4 suggestions introduced at the start of Round 2 with the AI-generated ideas label (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4).

arms.name: Late-AI Unlabeled
arms.description: No suggestions in Round 1; the same GPT-4 suggestions introduced at the start of Round 2 under Ideas from others (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4).

participants.exclusions: 254 adults initially enrolled; seven removed for failed attention checks or cursory responses, leaving the stated final sample of 247 (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.1). Section 3.6 also says outliers above three SDs and incomplete responses were removed, without counts or an explanation of whether these are the same exclusions (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283)). The assignment sentence follows the final-sample description, so the timing of exclusions and original allocation counts cannot be established; the arm counts are recorded as analyzed, not randomized. Reported one-way ANOVAs have F(4, 237), which does not reconcile with the stated final sample under the described model (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1); no alternative analyzed headcount is inferred.
participants.who: Adult convenience sample. Demographic screening aimed for diversity in age, gender, and education, but participant roles, recruitment source, and country are not reported. The population category cannot be confirmed from age diversity or web delivery alone. Twelve people from the main sample were invited to qualitative interviews, not an additional independent sample (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1-3.2; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4; PDF p. 7, Section 5).
participants.quote: A total of 254 adult participants were initially enrolled, and seven were removed for failing attention checks or offering cursory responses, resulting in a final sample size of 247.
participants.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1-3.2; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Sections 3.4 and 3.6; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 10286), Section 5

ai_tool.how_used: Participants received two or three pregenerated GPT-4 suggestions, each 30-50 words, at the assigned round, labeled AI-generated ideas or Ideas from others. The suggestions were lightly edited after pilot feedback for language consistency and factual accuracy. Participants typed their own responses; no open chatbot interaction is described (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.3-3.4). The embedding model scored participant-to-AI alignment and was not an assistance tool (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.5).

task.description: Propose innovative solutions to reduce plastic pollution in urban environments, then refine, expand, combine, or replace initial ideas in Round 2. Each round used an open text box; a minimum of 50 words per submission was enforced (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4). The brick Alternative Uses Task was a pre-treatment baseline measure, not an AI-treatment outcome.
task.duration: Two ideation rounds of 5-7 minutes each (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Figure 1; PDF p. 7, Section 5).

outcomes.name: Expert-rated overall creativity of the ideation submission, including change across rounds
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Modified Consensual Assessment Technique. Three experts in environmental policy or innovation management independently assessed final ideas on novelty, usefulness, and originality using 7-point scales; intraclass correlation >= 0.80. The formula combining these ratings into overall creativity and the aggregation across experts/ideas are not specified (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.5). The reported analyses use participant creativity scores; repeated measures are within participants. Section 3.5 describes final submissions, while Section 4.4 also analyzes Round 1 scores without separately describing their rating procedure. Final levels and round-to-round changes are retained as one outcome. Table 1 reports slopes of baseline AUT fluency on final creativity, not treatment effects: Control slope -0.012, SE 0.031, p = 0.687; Early-AI-Labeled 0.117, SE 0.035, p = 0.005; Early-AI-Unlabeled 0.159, SE 0.033, p < .001; Late-AI-Labeled 0.093, SE 0.037, p = 0.029; Late-AI-Unlabeled 0.118, SE 0.036, p = 0.005. The baseline-creativity-by-condition interaction is F(4, 237) = 4.42, p = .002; trust moderation is reported as p > .17 (PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.3, Table 1 and Figure 2d). These moderator statistics are not standardized AI effects. Figure 2 shows shaded 95% confidence intervals without numerical bounds (PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Figure 2 caption). Timing qualification: Late-AI participants received suggestions during Round 2, whereas Early-AI participants received them during Round 1 and continued in Round 2 without new external inputs. The document does not say whether earlier suggestions remained visible or were removed. Availability is coded mixed across the conditions/rounds; with_ai is directly supported for the Late-AI final output. An after_ai classification for the Early-AI final output cannot be confirmed (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4 and Figure 1).

contrasts.reported: Early-AI-Labeled M = 6.01, SD = 0.48; Control M = 4.94. Final-sample arm n = 49 and n = 50, respectively, are reported in Section 3.1. Descriptives are incomplete: Control SD and a numerical pairwise test, interval, or effect size are not supplied. Section 4.1 states that both Early-AI groups surpassed Control in post-hoc comparisons.

contrasts.control_arm: Late-AI Labeled and Late-AI Unlabeled (separate arms)
contrasts.reported: Post-hoc comparisons are described as showing that both Early-AI groups surpassed the Late-AI groups in overall creativity. The narrative does not provide numerical pairwise differences, standard errors, or adjusted p-values. This entry summarizes the stated comparisons; it is not a computed pooled contrast.

contrasts.reported: F(4, 237) = 37.54, p < .001, partial eta-squared = .38. This is the five-condition omnibus ANOVA, not an effect size or test for any one treatment-control contrast.

Creativity increases up to +0.88; t = -19.69, p < .001, d = 1.73. The text does not identify whether these statistics describe one Late-AI arm or the two arms together. Early-AI-Labeled improved by +0.17 and Control by +0.14. A repeated-measures ANOVA is described as confirming larger Late-AI improvements, but no F statistic or precision for the between-condition difference in change is printed. The reported d is a within-participant change effect, not a randomized between-arm effect.

outcomes.name: Semantic distance of participants' submissions from the supplied GPT-4 suggestions, including change across rounds
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each submission was embedded with text-embedding-ada-002 and compared with each GPT-4 suggestion using cosine similarity. Results are reported as semantic distance, with lower distance indicating stronger overlap (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.5). The transformation from cosine similarity to distance and the aggregation across suggestions are not specified. The paper analyzes a semantic-distance score for each participant submission; the number of underlying text pairs is not reported. This is alignment with AI exemplars, not similarity between different people, so it is not coded diversity or across_people. Final levels and within-participant changes are grouped as the same output measure. A process correlation with perceived external influence is r = -0.35, p < .001 (PDF p. 5 (printed p. 10284), Section 4.2 and Figure 2c); that self-report is not a separate scored-output outcome. Directions below refer to the reported distance scale; no signs or effect sizes have been recalculated. Timing qualification: Late-AI participants received suggestions during Round 2, whereas Early-AI participants received them during Round 1 and continued in Round 2 without new external inputs. The document does not say whether earlier suggestions remained visible or were removed. Availability is coded mixed across the conditions/rounds; with_ai is directly supported for the Late-AI final output. An after_ai classification for the Early-AI final output cannot be confirmed (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.4; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4 and Figure 1).

contrasts.reported: Semantic distance: Early-AI-Labeled M = 0.59; Control M = 0.84. Final-sample arm n = 49 and n = 50, respectively, appear in Section 3.1. Descriptives are incomplete: no SDs or numerical pairwise effect/precision are printed. Lower values mean stronger alignment to AI suggestions.

studies.label: Preparatory pilot for GPT-4 suggestion selection and editing

assignment.what_was_assigned: The paper describes a stimulus-checking pilot, without an allocation scheme, comparison conditions, or a human AI-assisted production task.

participants.exclusions: No exclusions or participant flow are described.
participants.who: A pilot is reported as n = 15, but the paragraph does not explicitly identify that n as people rather than stimuli/ratings and gives no participant description. A people count is therefore left null; the printed n is preserved in the quote. This pilot is not added to the main experimental sample.
participants.quote: Prior to finalizing these AI prompts, we conducted a small pilot study (n = 15) to verify that the suggestions were consistent in length, clarity, and perceived originality.

ai_tool.how_used: AI-generated suggestions were checked before the main experiment and lightly edited based on pilot feedback. They are the material being evaluated, not documented assistance for a human creative-production task (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.3).

task.description: Check consistency of AI suggestions in length, clarity, and perceived originality. Section 3.3 also says the suggestions were prerated for creativity (M = 5.3 on a 7-point scale), but does not clearly attribute that statistic to the pilot or specify the rating sample (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282)). No eligible outcome on human-produced creative work is reported.

company_involvement.description: Coauthor Yishan Huang is affiliated with Beijing Sankuai Network Technology Co., Ltd. No company funding or sponsor role is stated.

eligibility.reason: The main experiment explicitly randomly assigns people to GPT-4 suggestion timing/labeling conditions or a no-suggestion Control (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Sections 3.1-3.4); its reported final sample is 247 adults, above the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 3 (printed p. 10282), Section 3.1); domain experts score the creativity, novelty, usefulness, and originality of participants' submissions (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.5). Late-AI participants definitely receive suggestions while producing the final scored output (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 3.4), so eligibility does not depend on resolving Early-AI Round 2 access. This is assistance to human participants, not AI-versus-human output. The ANOVA/sample-count discrepancy prevents treating 247 as a verified model-specific N but does not supply a contrary count near the threshold. The pilot does not independently support core eligibility.

one_line_finding: Final expert-rated creativity was higher in Early-AI-Labeled (M = 6.01, SD = 0.48) than Control (M = 4.94), with an omnibus condition effect of F(4, 237) = 37.54, p < .001, partial eta-squared = .38 (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1).
open_questions: What were the original randomized total and allocation counts, and did exclusions occur before or after assignment? Section 3.1 reports a final sample of 247 after seven exclusions; Section 3.6 separately mentions outlier/incomplete-response removal (PDF pp. 3-4).

What analyzed samples or model terms explain the reported one-way ANOVA degrees of freedom F(4, 237), given the stated final sample and arm counts? No replacement participant count has been inferred (PDF p. 4, Section 4.1).

Were Early-AI suggestions still visible in Round 2? Without new external inputs does not establish withdrawal. Early-AI final-output classification as with_ai versus after_ai remains unresolved; Late-AI final outputs are clearly with_ai (PDF pp. 3-4, Section 3.4 and Figure 1).

What recruitment setting, participant population, and country apply? Web administration is stated, but an online-panel source and whether participants were remotely located or supervised are not (PDF p. 3, Section 3.3; PDF p. 7, Section 5).

How were expert ratings and any multiple ideas aggregated into the final participant creativity score, and how were Round 1 outputs rated? Complete arm means/SDs, numerical pairwise effects/intervals, and participant-level precision are needed for extraction (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.5-4.1; PDF p. 5, Figure 2).
How is semantic distance computed from cosine similarities and aggregated over AI suggestions? This measure does not compare outputs across people (PDF p. 4, Section 3.5).
Which Late-AI arm or aggregation has the reported increase up to +0.88, t = -19.69, d = 1.73, and semantic-distance change -0.23? The text does not resolve this (PDF p. 5, Section 4.4).
Does the pilot n = 15 denote people, and is the prerated suggestion creativity M = 5.3 derived from that pilot? Neither connection is explicitly stated (PDF p. 3, Section 3.3).
notes: Read the entire markdown conversion through the end of the references; the PDF has no included appendix. PDF text was checked for design, counts, measures, results, author affiliation, and version. Table 1 was additionally recovered with PyMuPDF find_tables using text strategy. S1 is the one main AI-assistance experiment; S2 records the explicitly named preparatory pilot because the form asks for one entry per study. Interviews are a subset of S1 rather than another independent sample. No reuse of another paper's participants is disclosed. Five scored-output measures are recorded. Overall creativity and semantic-distance trajectories are represented within their respective outcomes rather than counted again as separate measures. Novelty and originality remain separate because the paper rates and tests them separately. Baseline AUT fluency is a pretreatment covariate; perceived influence, creative self-efficacy, source recognition, response-time tracking, and qualitative themes are not added as scored creative-output outcomes. There is no direct across-people diversity measure and no confirmed AI-removal outcome. No primary outcome or preregistration is explicitly designated. Null population/structure/direction fields preserve information the paper does not give; omnibus tests cannot supply directional pairwise effects. The arm_means_sds_ns flags denote partially available descriptives only: the reported strings explicitly identify missing SDs, and arm counts are the reported final-sample counts, not verified model-specific Ns. No effect sizes, confidence intervals, graph values, pooled arm counts, or alternative analyzed counts were computed. Statistical signs and effect-size labels are retained as printed. No files in forms were read other than this completed output for validation.
